youtube.baslik: Tinnitus Retraining Therapy and the Jastreboff Model | Lesson 219 | AIHEAR Audiology Academy
youtube.aciklama:
Why does tinnitus bother some people so much, and how does TRT aim to change this? In this lesson we cover Jastreboff's neurophysiological model, the role of the limbic and autonomic systems, habituation of reaction and perception, the mixing point and sound therapy, the TRT categories and the level of evidence for the method.

AIHEAR Audiology Academy makes short, clear lessons for audiology students and professionals.

Sources: Jastreboff, Phantom auditory perception (tinnitus): mechanisms of generation and perception, Neuroscience Research (1990); Jastreboff and Hazell, Tinnitus Retraining Therapy: Implementing the Neurophysiological Model, Cambridge University Press (2004); Tinnitus Retraining Therapy Trial Research Group, Effect of Tinnitus Retraining Therapy vs Standard of Care on Tinnitus-Related Quality of Life, JAMA Otolaryngology Head and Neck Surgery (2019); Phillips and McFerran, Tinnitus Retraining Therapy (TRT) for tinnitus, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews (2010).

This video is for educational purposes and does not replace diagnosis or treatment.

cumleler: Hello, and welcome to the AIHEAR Audiology Academy.

cumleler.yazi: In this lesson we will learn about tinnitus retraining therapy, or TRT, and the neurophysiological model it is based on.
cumleler.ses: In this lesson we will learn about tinnitus retraining therapy, or T R T, and the neurophysiological model it is based on.

cumleler.yazi: We will cover the role of the limbic and autonomic systems, the goal of habituation, the TRT categories and the level of evidence.
cumleler.ses: We will cover the role of the limbic and autonomic systems, the goal of habituation, the T R T categories and the level of evidence.

cumleler.yazi: In the tinnitus lesson we briefly mentioned the neurophysiological model Jastreboff proposed in 1990; now let us look at it in detail.
cumleler.ses: In the tinnitus lesson we briefly mentioned the neurophysiological model Jastreboff proposed in nineteen ninety; now let us look at it in detail.

cumleler: In the model, the tinnitus signal often starts in the ear or lower auditory pathways, but this signal alone does not explain the problem.
The signal is first detected and processed at a subconscious level, then consciously perceived and evaluated in the auditory cortex.
What matters most is the link the signal forms with the limbic system, which regulates emotion, and the autonomic nervous system.
When these systems are engaged, the person feels anxiety, restlessness, sleep problems and poor concentration; tinnitus becomes distressing.

cumleler.yazi: Building on this model, Jastreboff and Hazell developed tinnitus retraining therapy, or TRT.
cumleler.ses: Building on this model, Jastreboff and Hazel developed tinnitus retraining therapy, or T R T.

cumleler: In this drawing we see the auditory pathway from the cochlea to the cortex.
The tinnitus signal can arise anywhere along this pathway, often with changes caused by hearing loss.
The model stresses that from the thalamus onward, the auditory pathway has rich connections with the limbic and autonomic systems.
Thanks to these connections, a sound such as an alarm or a baby crying makes us act at once.
If tinnitus is learned as a threat, the same connections keep pushing it to the foreground.
The model proposes that these connections can change, so the brain can reclassify tinnitus as an unimportant signal.
According to the model, the tinnitus signal is meaningless and neutral when it first appears.
If the signal is paired with fear, anxiety or a negative thought, for example taken as a sign of disease, it gains a negative meaning.
Thoughts such as "is tinnitus a sign of a brain tumor?" or "will I go deaf?" strengthen this pairing.
Over time the signal itself, even without the thought, triggers distress and a stress reaction; this is called a conditioned reflex.
Because this reflex works largely at a subconscious level, the person cannot ignore tinnitus even if they want to.

cumleler.yazi: The aim of TRT is to weaken this conditioned link, that is, to retrain the reflex.
cumleler.ses: The aim of T R T is to weaken this conditioned link, that is, to retrain the reflex.

cumleler.yazi: The goal of TRT is habituation, that is, the brain stops reacting to and noticing an unimportant signal.
cumleler.ses: The goal of T R T is habituation, that is, the brain stops reacting to and noticing an unimportant signal.

cumleler: The first stage is habituation of reaction: tinnitus is still heard, but no longer causes anxiety, stress or distress.
Think of the hum of a refrigerator; we can hear it, but it does not bother us and most of the time we do not notice it.
The second stage is habituation of perception: the person does not notice tinnitus most of the day, but hears it when they pay attention.
This approach does not aim to remove the loudness or the presence of tinnitus.
The measure of success is a reduced impact of tinnitus on the person's life.

cumleler.yazi: The principle of sound therapy in TRT is to avoid silence and reduce the contrast between tinnitus and outside sound.
cumleler.ses: The principle of sound therapy in T R T is to avoid silence and reduce the contrast between tinnitus and outside sound.

cumleler: This schematic graph shows how tinnitus becomes less salient as the external sound rises.
The level at which the external sound begins to blend with tinnitus is called the mixing point.

cumleler.yazi: In TRT, the sound generator is usually set at or slightly below this point, so tinnitus can still be heard.
cumleler.ses: In T R T, the sound generator is usually set at or slightly below this point, so tinnitus can still be heard.

cumleler: Covering tinnitus completely, that is, masking it, is not recommended, because the brain cannot habituate to a signal it does not hear.
The sound should also be pleasant or neutral, so that it does not itself cause discomfort.

cumleler.yazi: TRT has two core components: directive counseling and sound therapy.
cumleler.ses: T R T has two core components: directive counseling and sound therapy.

cumleler: In counseling, the person is shown with diagrams how the auditory system works, how tinnitus arises and why it became distressing.
The aim is for the person to truly understand that tinnitus is not dangerous, and for the negative meaning of the signal to dissolve.
Sound therapy reduces the salience of tinnitus by giving the brain a constant, neutral sound input.
Sound generators are usually worn in both ears, and they are recommended for most of the day.
Treatment is a long process; it usually lasts one to two years and includes regular follow-up visits.

maddeler.metin: How does the auditory system work?

cumleler: The counseling session starts with a simple explanation of the basic structure of the auditory system.
Next, it is explained that tinnitus is often the brain's response to small changes in the auditory system.
The link with the limbic and autonomic systems is explained with examples from the person's own experience.
It is stressed that habituation is a natural brain process and that we already habituate to many sounds in daily life.
Finally, the importance of avoiding silence and of sound therapy is explained.
This explanation is not given once and left; it is repeated at follow-up visits and the person's questions are answered.

cumleler.yazi: In TRT, people are placed in one of five categories at the first assessment; the category sets the approach.
cumleler.ses: In T R T, people are placed in one of five categories at the first assessment; the category sets the approach.

cumleler: In category zero, tinnitus has little impact on life; brief counseling is often enough.
In category one, tinnitus clearly affects life, without significant hearing loss or hyperacusis; counseling and a sound generator are used.
In category two, there is also a hearing loss that matters to the person; sound therapy is given mainly through hearing aids.
In category three, the main problem is hyperacusis; the sound generator starts at a very low level and is slowly raised to desensitize.
In category four, sound exposure worsens symptoms for a long time, for example until the next day; progress is slowest in this group.
The category is set through a structured interview and an audiological assessment.
The interview asks about the effect of tinnitus on sleep, concentration, work and social life.
The audiogram shows whether the person has a hearing loss that matters in daily life.

cumleler.yazi: Sound tolerance is explored; loudness discomfort level, or LDL, is measured carefully and with the person's consent.
cumleler.ses: Sound tolerance is explored; loudness discomfort level, or L D L, is measured carefully and with the person's consent.

cumleler: It is asked specifically whether symptoms increase for hours, or until the next day, after sound exposure.
The category can change during treatment; for example, when hyperacusis decreases, the person may move to another category.
A purely illustrative case: a fifty-five-year-old has a moderate high-frequency sensorineural loss in both ears.
The person says tinnitus makes it hard to fall asleep and to concentrate at work.
They describe no clear sensitivity to sound, and their symptoms do not stay worse for long after sound exposure.
They also say they struggle to follow conversation in crowded places, so the hearing loss matters to them.
This picture fits category two; alongside counseling, sound therapy is given mainly through hearing aids.
The aids both make speech easier to understand and raise ambient sound, reducing the contrast between tinnitus and silence.

cumleler.yazi: Observational studies from TRT centers have reported clear improvement in a large share of patients.
cumleler.ses: Observational studies from T R T centers have reported clear improvement in a large share of patients.

cumleler: But without a control group, it is hard to know how much of the improvement comes from the method itself.

cumleler.yazi: In 2019, a US placebo-controlled multicenter trial compared full TRT, counseling with a placebo generator, and standard care.
cumleler.ses: In twenty nineteen, a US placebo-controlled multicenter trial compared full T R T, counseling with a placebo generator, and standard care.

cumleler: Questionnaires measuring tinnitus impact showed no significant difference between the three groups; many participants improved in each.

cumleler.yazi: A Cochrane review also reported that the evidence for the effectiveness of TRT is limited.
cumleler.ses: A Cochrane review also reported that the evidence for the effectiveness of T R T is limited.

cumleler: These results suggest that counseling and regular follow-up carry an important share of the improvement.

cumleler.yazi: The education-based counseling part of TRT is in line with the guideline recommendations we saw in the tinnitus management lesson.
cumleler.ses: The education-based counseling part of T R T is in line with the guideline recommendations we saw in the tinnitus management lesson.

cumleler: The neurophysiological model is still used in many clinics today to explain tinnitus to the person.
Advice to avoid silence and to use sound enrichment is also widely applied.
Cognitive behavioral therapy remains the psychological approach with the strongest evidence.

cumleler.yazi: If there is marked anxiety or depression, the person is referred to the appropriate specialist, even if TRT is being used.
cumleler.ses: If there is marked anxiety or depression, the person is referred to the appropriate specialist, even if T R T is being used.

sahneler.metin: Do not give counseling once and leave it. Have the person explain the model in their own words; misunderstood information does not reduce anxiety.
cumleler: A tip from the clinic: at the end of the counseling session, ask the person to explain the model in their own words.
That way you see right away what was understood and what was misunderstood.
A misunderstood point, such as the idea that tinnitus shows brain damage, keeps feeding anxiety.
Reinforce the same topic with brief repetitions at follow-up visits.

maddeler.metin: Counseling and sound at mixing point

cumleler: In the Jastreboff model, what makes tinnitus distressing is the conditioned link the signal forms with the limbic and autonomic systems.

cumleler.yazi: The goal of TRT is not to erase the sound, but to bring about habituation of reaction first, then of perception.
cumleler.ses: The goal of T R T is not to erase the sound, but to bring about habituation of reaction first, then of perception.

cumleler: The method combines directive counseling with sound therapy set at or slightly below the mixing point.

cumleler.yazi: People are placed in categories from zero to four; controlled trials have not shown an added benefit of TRT.
cumleler.ses: People are placed in categories from zero to four; controlled trials have not shown an added benefit of T R T.

sahneler.soru: At what level is the TRT sound generator usually set?
secenekler: At or below the mixing point
sahneler.aciklama: Tinnitus should still be heard; the brain cannot habituate to a signal it does not hear.

cumleler.yazi: Test yourself: in tinnitus retraining therapy, at what level is the sound generator usually set?

cumleler: The correct answer is B: at or slightly below the mixing point.
At this level tinnitus is still heard; the aim is not to mask it, but to help the brain habituate to the signal.
